spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns default 25. Spirals in practice manifest well before that
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:84 `for ti in range(opts.max_turns):` bounds the loop; `else: tr.stop_reason = tr.stop_reason or "max_turns"` (runner.py ~165). config.py:29 `max_turns: int = 25`, threaded into RunnerOptions at orchestrator.py:73-77, default 25, configs/cheap.json sets 18. Cap is checked and ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end; the dominant stop. Drives execution termination.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: hard cap. Spirals usually manifest well before 25 turns.

spec_features.feature_name: wall-clock backstop + two no-tool turns + stuck detector
spec_features.spec_quote: a wall-clock backstop, two consecutive no-tool turns, or (optionally) a stuck detector
spec_features.evidence: Wall-clock: runner.py:89-91 `if time.time() - tr.started_at > opts.max_wall_s: tr.stop_reason = "wall_clock"; break` (max_wall_s=600.0 default, runner.py:53 — note: not configurable, orchestrator does not pass it, but default still runs and breaks). Two no-tool turns: runner.py ~158 `if not step.tool_calls and ti > 0 and not tr.turns[-2].tool_calls: tr.stop_reason = "no_tool_calls"; break`. Stuck detector: runner.py ~148 `if (opts.early_stop_on_spiral and spiral_onset_turn is not None and ti - spiral_onset_turn >= opts.spiral_tail_turns): break`.
spec_features.notes: All three branches actually break the loop. Wall-clock uses the hardcoded default (not config-exposed) but still executes. Stuck detector is gated on early_stop_on_spiral (default False) but is genuinely wired and enabled by configs/cheap.json.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No tool calls at all for two turns running => model is just emitting text; end to avoid burning tokens.

spec_features.feature_name: stuck detector: mark onset, run spiral_tail_turns more, then stop
spec_features.spec_quote: once the run is "in trouble" ... we mark the onset turn, then run spiral_tail_turns ... more turns ... and stop
spec_features.evidence: Onset marked: runner.py ~140 `if in_trouble and spiral_onset_turn is None: spiral_onset_turn = ti` where in_trouble = consecutive_failures>=failure_threshold OR repeat_streak>=failure_threshold. Tail-then-stop: runner.py ~148 `if (opts.early_stop_on_spiral and spiral_onset_turn is not None and ti - spiral_onset_turn >= opts.spiral_tail_turns): tr.stop_reason = "stuck_detector"; break`. spiral_tail_turns=4, failure_threshold=4 threaded from config (orchestrator.py:74-76). configs/cheap.json enables early_stop_on_spiral=true.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and executes when early_stop_on_spiral is on. The tail-capture logic is implemented as described.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Set `early_stop_on_spiral=True` to cut runs short and save tokens once the spiral is confirmed and a minimum tail has been captured.

spec_features.spec_quote: permission_to_stop (explicitly legitimizes giving up when a task looks infeasible)
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPTS['permission_to_stop'] delivers real instruction text ('some tasks turn out to be infeasible... That is not your fault... it is correct and expected to call `submit` with status giving_up'). Delivered as the system message in runner.py via get_system_prompt(system_prompt_id). The referenced `submit`/'giving_up' tool is fully built (tools.py TOOL_SCHEMAS submit with enum [done, giving_up]) and honored as a stop in runner.py (status=='giving_up' -> stop_reason='model_gave_up'; break). Wired into the A/B at configs/mitigation_ab.json system_prompt_ids includes 'permission_to_stop'.
spec_features.notes: Real text whose referenced exit tool is fully implemented and honored, and it is actually exercised by a shipped config. End-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: permission_to_stop: explicitly tells the model it's fine to stop and report that the task may be infeasible -- a candidate *mitigation* to A/B test.

spec_features.spec_quote: submit is the only legitimate exit. The model ends a run by claiming done or giving_up
spec_features.evidence: runner.py submit handling: `if tc["name"] == "submit": status = ...; tr.stop_reason = ("model_claimed_done" if status == "done" else "model_gave_up"); ... done = True` then `if done: break`. Both done and giving_up terminate the loop. submit schema exists (tools.py) and executor.execute echoes it while the runner controls termination (tools.py: 'Handled by the runner (controls loop termination)').
spec_features.notes: The model can end its own run via giving_up, which is honored as a hard stop. Genuine self-exit path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This gives us a clean, model-reported completion signal -- and `giving_up` is itself part of the degradation signal. (and the giving_up branch is a measured signal, not framed as protection)
